units.source_text: 这信写在一张一摺的青色纸上，字体都是草书，

en.t: The letter was written on a single folded sheet of blue paper, and all the characters were in cursive script,

units.source_text: 写得剑拔弩张，却并无根据，只是信手挥舞，

en.t: written with a fierce, overstrained flourish, yet with no real foundation, merely waved about at random,

units.source_text: 把“し”字写得极长，故意装腔作势。

en.t: with the character “し” drawn out extremely long, deliberately putting on airs.

units.source_text: 行间亦不整齐，斜向一边，形似欲倒。

en.t: The lines were uneven as well, slanting to one side as if they were about to topple over.

units.source_text: 但近江君很得意，自己笑着欣赏了一番。

en.t: But Omi no Kimi was very pleased with it and admired it for a while, smiling to herself.

units.source_text: 毕竟她也懂得女子书简的格式，把信卷得很细小，

en.t: After all, she did know the proper form for a woman’s letter, and she rolled the letter up very small,

units.source_text: 系在一枝抚子花上，派一个新来的女童送去。

en.t: tied it to a stem of pinks, and sent it off with a newly arrived young girl.

units.source_text: 这女童虽是打扫厕所的，却很伶俐，又长得漂亮。

en.t: Although this girl was assigned to clean the lavatories, she was clever and also quite pretty.

units.source_text: 她走到弘徽殿女御的饮食室中，对侍女们说：

en.t: She went to the dining room of the Kokiden Consort and said to the ladies-in-waiting,

units.source_text: “请将此信呈送女御。”

en.t: “Please present this letter to Her Highness.”

units.source_text: 打杂差的侍女认得这女童，知道她是北厅里的侍童，便收了信。

en.t: The maid on miscellaneous duty recognized the girl and knew she was a child attendant from the northern hall, so she accepted the letter.

units.source_text: 一个名叫大辅君的侍女拿了信走进去，呈与女御，

en.t: A lady-in-waiting named Taifu no Kimi took the letter inside and presented it to the Consort,

units.source_text: 又把信从花枝上解下，请她阅读。

en.t: then untied it from the flower branch and asked her to read it.

units.source_text: 女御看了一遍，微笑着放下了信。

en.t: The Consort read it through once, then set the letter down with a smile.

units.source_text: 有一个叫作中纳言的贴身侍女，从旁窥看，对女御说：

en.t: A close attendant called Chunagon peered at it from the side and said to the Consort,

units.source_text: “这封信时髦得很啊。”

en.t: “This letter is terribly fashionable.”

units.source_text: 她想再细看看。

en.t: She wanted to look at it more closely.

units.source_text: 女御说：“恐是我看不懂草体字之故吧，

en.t: The Consort said, “Perhaps it is because I cannot make out the cursive writing,

units.source_text: 这首诗似乎本末不称呢。”

en.t: but this poem seems rather mismatched from beginning to end.”

units.source_text: 便把信递给中纳言，对她说道：

en.t: Then she handed the letter to Chunagon and said to her,

units.source_text: “回信也要写得如此大模大样。

en.t: “The reply must be written in just this same grand style.

units.source_text: 不然，要被人看轻为下品。

en.t: Otherwise people will look down on us as vulgar.

units.source_text: 你立刻替我写吧。”

en.t: Write it for me at once.”

units.source_text: 她叫中纳言代笔。

en.t: She had Chunagon write it on her behalf.

units.source_text: 众青年侍女觉得此信稀奇，都低声窃笑。

en.t: The young ladies-in-waiting all found the letter odd and whispered with suppressed laughter.

units.source_text: 女童催索回信了。

en.t: The girl began pressing them for a reply.

units.source_text: 中纳言告女御：“这封信里引用了许多风雅的典故，

en.t: Chunagon told the Consort, “This letter cites many elegant allusions,

units.source_text: 回信很难写。

en.t: so a reply will be very difficult to write.

units.source_text: 叫人代笔，似乎失礼吧。”

en.t: Would it not seem rude to have someone else write it?”

units.source_text: 便模仿女御的笔迹写了：“相隔甚近，而一向疏远，诚为恨事。

en.t: Then, imitating the Consort’s handwriting, she wrote: “Though we are separated by so little, we have long remained distant, which I deeply regret.
